description: The status of one submission — YOUR human's, never anybody else's. No token required. Two ways in: a signed-in identity resolves its own record with no id at all, or `submission_id` plus the `claim_token` handed back once at submit time opens the record that token belongs to. An id ALONE never works: ids travel through URLs and chat logs, and if an id were a credential every stranger's answers would be readable by anyone who ever saw a link. A wrong id, a wrong token and an id that was never issued all return the same `found: false`, so this cannot be used to test which ids exist. What comes back is status, dates and failed gates — never the answers as stored, never the reviewer's private note. Args: { form_id, submission_id?, claim_token? }. Returns: { ok, found, submission? }. No auth required.

claim_token.description: The one-time token returned at submit. Must be sent WITH submission_id; either alone does nothing.

submission_id.description: Needed only when reading by claim token rather than by identity.

name: ic_forms_my_submission

outputSchema.description: The tool's JSON result. Every field the tool's description names is present at the top level; ok, error and error_kind follow the shared envelope.

error.description: Why the call failed, in a sentence a person can act on. Present only when ok is false.

error_kind.description: Machine-readable failure class: no_token, missing_scope, forbidden, not_found, invalid_input, rate_limited or transient

ok.description: true when the call did what it was asked; false with `error` and `error_kind` when it did not

result.description: The tool's value when it returns a list or a single value instead of an object

text.description: The tool's reply when it returns plain text instead of JSON

title: Read your OWN submission to a form
